utterances.text: Which means that if I bring you witnesses who will confirm that they had talks with Mr. Novakovic, and his secretary, and that what you are saying is not correct, is not true, will that mean that that witness is not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the form of the question. He is asking him to comment on future witnesses and how they will testify. It's inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I will change my question. So it means that if somebody says that it is as it is, as I have asked you now, that person would not be telling the truth. Is that all right? Is the question all right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Same objection. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Very well. You therefore maintain that Mr. Novakovic was completely sober when you talked to him?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: He appeared completely sober when I spoke with him, yes, and he didn't drink in my presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: In your presence. Yes. That's what I am asking you. In your presence Mr. Novakovic did not drink?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: Not alcohol, no. Coffee, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Alcohol. That's what I am referring to. Yes. Coffee, water, juice, that's a different matter. That's all right now. I have the right to a rejoinder, and in June you will hear the real truth of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Objection. That's argument coming from Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's not an argument. I am just telling you that I shall be having a witness -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You are announcing the calling of a rejoinder witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Just one more question. Yes, I say that I will have a witness to discuss this question. That's right. And he is going to explain the question in hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: One last question. Do you feel any personal interest in this particular case? You arrested Mr. Dokmanovic deceitfully?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: Mr. Dokmanovic -- (answer obscured by translation).

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: You made him cross the border, you said that he would be received by Mr. Klein. You lured him across the border. You lured him to cross the border; is that true?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: (Answer obscured by translation).

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Enticed him?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: -- Across the border. He made the decision himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: But you lured him into thinking that he would be going to a meeting with Mr. Klein?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Fila --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I withdraw the question. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Do you show, therefore, any personal interest in showing that you have brought the wrong man?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: My personal interest is to present the facts and let the judges decide on the decisions. I have no bias personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Curtis. I only asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No offence meant. My objection about the documents remains, is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Mr. Fila does not want the documents in, we will withdraw them. He was proposing that they be shown to the court. We have no problem with withdrawing them, if he doesn't want them to go in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, are we talking about both the notes and the typewritten report? Are you objecting to the typewritten report?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I am objecting to the report because it was cut up and I don't know what it says, really. So it's not evidence. And if he could corroborate that these were his notes, then I would accept them. But the report cannot be proof, some kind of internal report, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, he is -- the witness testified that this is the report that he has prepared, and I think it corroborates his testimony. So, to this that extent, we would offer it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I forgot one particular question. You mentioned something about Vodicka. The Prosecutor didn't ask you, but it remained here in writing, it wasn't crossed out. The name of Vodicka was mentioned. So could you please look at the report and say what you meant, its the last page I think, I think. The Prosecutor didn't ask about this, so I forgot to put a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: What is this about? Did Dokmanovic tell you about this? I mean, sorry, Novakovic, sorry?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: What's in my report Mr. Novakovic told me. I'll read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Please read it.

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: "I am also aware that Slavko used his influence to arrange for a Croatian women called Vodicka to escape from Ilok and cross the border into Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Fila's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I must raise an objection when Mr. Fila addresses the court and argues his point after he asks questions. This is not the appropriate time to put forth arguments to the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So we have decided to admit document P212 into evidence. The typewritten report by Mr. Curtis, it is admitted into evidence, as well as the other one, the handwritten notes, Prosecutor Exhibit 211. Mr. Williamson, any --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Mr. Curtis, at the conclusion of this interview, did you go out to dinner with Mr. Novakovic at his invitation?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: Yes. During the course of the interview, just to clarify this point, I asked Mr. Novakovic if it was possible to see the bridge that crosses between Backa Palanka and Ilok, because, of course, it's coming to our inquiries a lot but not easy to get to. He made a phone call and he said that it would be arranged. In actual fact, we went to a restaurant near to the bridge, but two or three hundred metres away, where he said he invited us for lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And during this lunch or dinner, was alcohol consumed at that time?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Okay. This was after the interview had been concluded?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And at that time did Mr. Novakovic, in your estimation, become intoxicated?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: He most certainly did. I would say that he went over the top with the alcohol. And my impression was in a macho way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Is the fact that he became physically sick?

utterances.speaker: KEVIN CURTIS
utterances.text: I am aware that he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just say one thing. My job, as an investigator, and all the investigators here does include giving testimony before the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if there is an issue about us reconvening. If the only reason that we are reconvening is for Mr. Fila to present this coat to the court, we have no objection of that being done out of our presence, and then it can be formally admitted in June, when we reconvene. If there are other matters, then, fine, but if that's the only issue that is before the court, we have no objection to that being done outside our presence, and being done outside a formal sitting of the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, do you think by 4.30 you could come here with the jacket and the diary?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that depends on God and Yugoslav Airlines. If Yugoslav Airlines lands, and if God permits this, then the plane should come. I mean, JAT is the name of our airline, Yugoslav airlines and they say this is an abbreviation for "joke about time," it's spelt J-A-T.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right, but in principle, it should land at what --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It should have landed already, now, at 20 past 12. Now it is supposed to have landed. And I am going to bring this for sure -- I'm sorry. And I promise the agendas, and I told them to take the agendas. Mr. Curtis saw these agendas too, when he talked. I mean, this is not part of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Two points. First of all, we want to receive this evidence in court, and with the Prosecutor, with both parties present, of course. And we -- since we have a hearing on a different case at 3.30, which should be over, but we should be through by 4.30, we could reconvene at 4.30, if this is convenient to both parties? Is it fine with you, Mr. Fila, 4.30?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Quite all right. But perhaps we can bring it in at 3.00, so that you wouldn't be bothered to stay later. Because, really, it only takes five minutes. I just hand it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour, 3.00 or 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: 3.00 is perhaps better, we can give it to you at 3.00 and then you can continue at 3.30, if it's easier for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I think, for a lot of practical reasons, it would be better to stick to the 4.30 suggestion, if you don't mind. 4.30. It will take probably 15 minutes. There are practical problems, otherwise. All right. 4.30. All right. So we'll adjourn now. Sorry. I forgot. I am a bit exhausted, sir. I should ask the parties whether there is any objection to the witness being released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Curtis, thank you so much for your patience, also for giving evidence in court, and you may now be released. And we adjourn until 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: --- Upon adjourning at 12.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We, of course, regret this delay. It is not our fault. And I'm afraid that we had another case. I am sorry for any inconvenience this may have caused you. Let us start right away. Mr. Fila, have you all the relevant --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This is the agenda that we talked about. It has the 19th. I showed the Prosecution. The 19th of November, the government meeting, the accused, Mr. Dokmanovic, can read out this. Then the next relevant date is the 3rd of December, and the 4th of December onwards. I would like you personally to have a look at this, and would the usher show you the agenda, and Mr. Dokmanovic can read it out and identify it, or anybody who can read it in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Fila is correct. He did show it to us and we had a chance to look through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: On the 19th, it says the government meeting in Erdut. If that is relevant for the Court. It says, as I say, that the 19th of November is the government meeting in Erdut -- no, just the government meeting on the 19th of November. It doesn't say where it is, just that it is a government meeting on the 19th of November. The next day, on the 19th, he writes about the meeting, and it says that on the next day, at 12.00 in Vukovar, at the VELEPROMET compound is the government meeting. And then the next date is the 3rd of December. I don't know whether that helps you at all. I don't think it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The second thing you asked for, here it is. The accused is ready to put it on, if you would like to see it on him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Shall we call it -- are you producing this as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this could be perhaps D2a Exhibit D2a because it was in the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Your Honours, would you like Mr. Dokmanovic to wear the shirt, the vest, and the jacket? No?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I suggest, in terms of the reference number, I think it was given a number 2a. I believe Exhibit D2 was the videotape, maybe it would be more appropriate to be 48a. 48 was the other clothing, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, D48. I beg your pardon. Yes, you're quite right. (Mr. Dokmanovic puts on jacket).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dokmanovic, thank you. I wonder whether there are any matters to be discussed. May I simply then again repeat one point I made this morning, I think, namely, that we intend to come to an end of this trial on the 26th of June. So therefore, it is in the best interests of the accused and so therefore I very much urge the -- I would like to urge the Prosecutor to make an effort to compress as much as possible the testimony. Otherwise, we will have to shorten, as I said, the time for the closing statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the things that we have discussed in the interim, between this morning's session and now, and I discussed this with Mr. Niemann when he was on break, is we will try to submit as detailed reports as we can from any experts that we would call, so that if it were necessary to call them, we can perhaps try to limit their questioning to a very short period, and perhaps condense it down even more than we had anticipated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. And, of course, as for the possible visit to Vukovar, we will decide towards the end of that week. But if you can make also an effort -- again, for the sake of saving time -- if you may submit your closing statements in writing. I think Mr. Fila promised to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, quite definitely. But Mr. Niemann asked some time for something, I'm not quite clear on what he wanted, but, yes, whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will make a written submission as well, though we would like to, I think, have some oral argument on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: And again, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No, that was not it. Mr. Niemann -- I apologise for interrupting, Mr. Williamson -- but as we were discussing these matters, Mr. Niemann said something we should hand something in simultaneously. It was a question of time. And I did not understand what he had in mind, what Mr. Niemann had in mind, what the proposal is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It was very clear -- I mean, Mr. Williamson, you made --

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, I think Mr. Niemann's point was, in terms of closing argument, that it should be simultaneously, we should have the same deadline so in effect one argument is not a response to the other argument, because we both get an opportunity for rebuttal and rejoinder, as I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Do you think that one day could be sufficient for both parties because this could be Friday and then we could ask you to submit by Thursday afternoon the two closing statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, that's all right. That's agreeable. Very well. I think I'll be able to wind up in one day, on Monday, my evidence. We're working all day, so I think that will be enough. So I should like to ask Mr. Williamson to be ready on Tuesday with his evidence, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: That's fine. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: We've cleaned up all those matters now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: We will be submitting the statements on Thursday. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So Thursday by 5.00. If the two statements could be submitted simultaneously, by Thursday, so on Friday you can sum up your arguments and then we may ask questions. All right. We can now adjourn. Again, I apologise for the delay, and we will reconvene on the 22nd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: At what time, Your Honours? At what time, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: MR. WILLIAMSON
utterances.text: At what time is the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: At what time? At 9.30, I think, as usual. 9.30. I think this is the usual schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 5.33 p.m. until 22nd June, 1998, at 9.30 a.m.
